title.zh: 卷六十五 列傳第二十五 吉翰 劉道產 杜驥 申恬
title.en: Volume 65 Biographies 25: Ji Han, Liu Daochan, Du Ji, Shen Tian
title.raw: 卷六十五 列傳第二十五 吉翰 劉道產 杜驥 申恬 Volume 65 Biographies 25: Ji Han, Liu Daochan, Du Ji, Shen Tian

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十五 吉翰 劉道產 杜驥 申恬

translations.literal: Biography 25: Ji Han, Liu Daochan, Du Ji, Shen Tian
translations.idiomatic: Biography 25 — Ji Han, Liu Daochan, Du Ji, and Shen Tian

sentences.zh: 吉翰，字休文，馮翊池陽人也。

translations.literal: Ji Han, style name Xiuwen, was a native of Chiyang in Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Han, whose courtesy name was Xiuwen, came from Chiyang in Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 初為龍驤將軍道憐參軍，隨府轉征虜左軍參軍，員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: At first he was aide to General of the Soaring Dragon Daolian; with the headquarters he was transferred to aide of the Left Army of the Vanquisher of Barbarians, then External Gentleman Attendant-at-Court.
translations.idiomatic: He began as an aide on the staff of General of the Soaring Dragon Liu Daolian, then moved with the command to aide of the Left Army of the Vanquisher of Barbarians and finally to external attendant gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 隨道憐北征廣固，賜爵建城縣五等男。

translations.literal: He accompanied Daolian on the northern campaign to Guanggu and was enfeoffed as fifth-rank baron of Jiancheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Daolian north to campaign at Guanggu and was granted the fifth-rank barony of Jiancheng County.

sentences.zh: 轉道憐驃騎中兵參軍，從事中郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Central Army Aide on Daolian's Flying Cavalry staff and then Attending Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to central army aide on Daolian's Flying Cavalry staff and then to attending gentleman.

sentences.zh: 為將佐十餘年，清謹剛正，甚為高祖所知賞。

translations.literal: For more than ten years he served as a military officer, pure, careful, and upright; the Founding Emperor knew and valued him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: For over a decade he served as a military officer, noted for his integrity and strict probity, and won high esteem from the Founding Emperor.

sentences.zh: 永初三年，轉道憐太尉司馬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu he became Chief of Staff to Daolian as Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongchu (422) he became chief of staff to Daolian in his capacity as Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉元年，出督梁南秦二州諸軍事、龍驤將軍、西戎校尉、梁南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, Han was sent out to supervise military affairs in Liang and Nanqin provinces, as General of the Soaring Dragon, Colonel of the Western Rong, and Inspector of Liang and Nanqin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanjia (424) under Emperor Wen, Han was sent out to supervise military affairs in Liang and Nanqin, with the titles General of the Soaring Dragon, Colonel of the Western Rong, and inspector of both provinces.

sentences.zh: 三年，仇池氐楊興平遣使歸順，并兒弟為質，翰遣始平太守龐諮據武興。

translations.literal: In the third year, Yang Xingping of the Qiuchi Di sent envoys to submit, presenting his sons and younger brothers as hostages; Han sent Shiping Administrator Pang Zi to hold Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (426), Yang Xingping of the Qiuchi Di sent envoys to submit, presenting his sons and younger brothers as hostages; Han sent Shiping administrator Pang Zi to hold Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 仇池大帥楊玄遣弟難當率眾拒諮，又遣將強鹿皮向白水。

translations.literal: Qiuchi chieftain Yang Xuan sent his brother Nandang with troops to resist Zi, and also sent the general Qiang Lupi toward Baishui.
translations.idiomatic: Qiuchi chieftain Yang Xuan sent his brother Nandang with troops to resist Zi, and also sent the general Qiang Lupi toward Baishui.

sentences.zh: 諮擊破，難當等並退走。

translations.literal: Zi defeated them, and Nandang and the others all retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Zi defeated them, and Nandang and the others all retreated.

sentences.zh: 其年，徙督益寧二州梁州之巴西梓潼宕渠南漢中秦州之安固懷寧六郡諸軍事、益州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: That same year he was transferred to supervise military affairs in Yi and Ning provinces and the six commanderies of Baxi, Zitong, Dangqu, Southern Hanzhong, Angu, and Huaining in Liang and Qin, and made Inspector of Yi Province, his general's rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was transferred to supervise military affairs in Yi and Ning and the six commanderies of Baxi, Zitong, Dangqu, Southern Hanzhong, Angu, and Huaining in Liang and Qin, and made inspector of Yi Province, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 在益州著美績，甚得方伯之體，論者稱之。

translations.literal: In Yi Province he achieved distinguished merit, fully embodying the model of a regional governor, and commentators praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In Yi Province he achieved distinguished merit, fully embodying the model of a regional governor, and commentators praised him.

sentences.zh: 六年，以老疾徵還，除彭城王義康司徒司馬，加輔國將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was recalled due to age and illness, appointed Chief of Staff to the Minister over the Masses under Prince of Pengcheng Liu Yikang, and given the additional title General Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (429) he was recalled due to age and illness, appointed chief of staff to the Minister over the Masses under Prince of Pengcheng Liu Yikang, and given the additional title General Who Supports the State.

sentences.zh: 時太祖經略河南，以翰為持節、監司、雍、并三州諸軍事、司州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was planning operations in Henan, Han was made Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of military affairs in Si, Yong, and Bing provinces, and Inspector of Si Province, his general's rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Wen was laying plans for Henan, Han was appointed bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs in Si, Yong, and Bing, and inspector of Si Province, retaining his existing general's rank.

sentences.zh: 會前鋒諸軍到彥之等敗退，明年，復為司徒司馬，將軍如故。

translations.literal: When the vanguard armies under Dao Yanzhi and others were defeated and withdrew, the following year he was again made Chief of Staff to the Minister over the Masses, his general's rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: After the vanguard under Dao Yanzhi and others was routed and pulled back, the next year he was again made chief of staff to the Minister over the Masses, with his general's rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 其年，又假節、監徐、兗二州、豫州之梁郡諸軍事、徐州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: That same year he was also granted provisional staff authority as Supervisor of military affairs in Xu and Yan provinces and Liang commandery in Yu Province, and Inspector of Xu Province, his general's rank still unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he received provisional staff authority as supervisor of military affairs in Xu and Yan and in Liang commandery of Yu, and was made inspector of Xu Province, while keeping his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 時有死罪囚，典籤意欲活之，因翰八關齋呈其事。

translations.literal: At the time there was a prisoner condemned to death; a registry clerk wished to save him and, while Han was observing the eight precepts fast, had the matter presented to him.
translations.idiomatic: There was then a prisoner under sentence of death whom a registry clerk hoped to spare; while Han was observing the eight precepts fast, the clerk had the case brought before him.

sentences.zh: 翰省訖，語「今且去，明可便呈」。

translations.literal: When Han had reviewed it, he said, "Go for now; you may present it tomorrow."
translations.idiomatic: After reviewing the petition, Han told him, "Leave for now—you may submit it tomorrow."

sentences.zh: 明旦，典籤不敢復入，呼之乃來。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day the clerk did not dare enter again; only when summoned did he come.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning the clerk did not dare come in again; he appeared only when called.

sentences.zh: 取昨所呈事視訖，謂之曰：「卿意當欲宥此囚死命。

translations.literal: Han took the document presented the day before, read it through, and said to him: "You surely mean to spare this prisoner his life.
translations.idiomatic: Han took up yesterday's petition, read it through, and said, "You mean to spare this man from execution.

sentences.zh: 昨於齋坐見其事，亦有心活之。

translations.literal: Yesterday in my fasting hall when I saw this matter, I too was minded to let him live.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday, when I saw the case in my fasting hall, I too was inclined to let him live.

sentences.zh: 但此囚罪重，不可全貸，既欲加恩，卿便當代任其罪。」

translations.literal: But this prisoner's crime is grave and cannot be fully pardoned; since you wish to show favor, you yourself must answer for his crime."
translations.idiomatic: But his crime is too grave for a full pardon; if you wish to show him mercy, you must bear the penalty in his place."

sentences.zh: 因命左右收典籤付獄殺之，原此囚生命。

translations.literal: He then ordered his attendants to seize the clerk, hand him over to prison, and execute him, while sparing the prisoner's life.
translations.idiomatic: He then had his attendants seize the clerk, send him to prison, and put him to death, while sparing the condemned prisoner.

sentences.zh: 其刑政如此，其下畏服，莫敢犯禁。

translations.literal: Such was his administration of punishment; those below feared and submitted, and none dared violate his prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the sternness of his justice: his subordinates feared him and none dared break his rules.

sentences.zh: 明年卒官，時年六十。

translations.literal: The following year he died in office, at the age of sixty.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he died in office, at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 追贈征虜將軍，持節、監、刺史如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given the title General Who Punishes the Barbarians, with staff authority, supervisory duties, and inspectorship recorded as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General Who Punishes the Barbarians, with his staff, supervisory, and inspector titles recorded as before.

sentences.zh: 劉道產，彭城呂人，太尉諮議參軍簡之子也。

translations.literal: Liu Daochan was a man of Lu in Pengcheng, son of Jian, a consulting aide to the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daochan, a native of Lu in Pengcheng, was the son of Jian, consulting aide to the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 簡之事在弟子康祖傳。

translations.literal: Jian's career is recorded in the biography of his younger brother Kangzu.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's career is told in the biography of his younger brother Kangzu.

sentences.zh: 道產初為輔國參軍，無錫令，在縣有能名。

translations.literal: Daochan first served as aide to the State-Supporting General, then as magistrate of Wuxi, where he gained a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: Daochan first served as aide to the State-Supporting General, then as magistrate of Wuxi, where he earned a name for capable administration.

sentences.zh: 高祖版為中軍行參軍，又為道憐驃騎參軍，襲父爵晉安縣五等侯。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor appointed him acting aide on the Central Army staff, then aide on Daolian's Flying Cavalry staff; he inherited his father's fifth-rank marquisate of Jin'an County.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor made him acting aide on the central army staff and then aide on Daolian's Flying Cavalry staff; he inherited his father's fifth-rank marquisate of Jin'an County.

sentences.zh: 廣州群盜因刺史謝道欣死為寇，攻沒州城，道憐加道產振武將軍南討，會始興謙之已平廣州，道產未至而反。

translations.literal: Bandits in Guangzhou, taking advantage of the death of Inspector Xie Daoxin, rose as marauders and captured the prefectural city; Daolian promoted Daochan to General Who Quells Martial Disorders and sent him south to attack, but by the time he arrived Qianzhi of Shixing had already pacified Guangzhou, and Daochan turned back before reaching it.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits in Guangzhou seized the prefectural city after Inspector Xie Daoxin's death, Daolian promoted Daochan to General Who Quells Martial Disorders and sent him south; but Qianzhi of Shixing had already pacified Guangzhou before Daochan arrived, and he turned back.

sentences.zh: 元年，除寧遠將軍、巴西、梓潼二郡太守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanjia he was made General of Distant Pacification and Administrator of the two commanderies of Baxi and Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanjia (424) he was appointed General of Distant Pacification and concurrent administrator of Baxi and Zitong.

sentences.zh: 郡人黃公生、任肅之、張石之等竝譙縱餘燼，與姻親侯攬、羅奧等招引白水氐，規欲為亂。

translations.literal: Huang Gongsheng, Ren Suzhi, Zhang Shizhi, and others of the commandery were all embers left from Qiao Zong's rebellion; with kinsmen Hou Lan, Luo Ao, and others they recruited the Baishui Di and plotted revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Gongsheng, Ren Suzhi, Zhang Shizhi, and others in the commandery were remnants of Qiao Zong's revolt; with relatives Hou Lan and Luo Ao they stirred up the Baishui Di and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 道產誅公生等二十一家，宥其餘黨。

translations.literal: Daochan executed Gongsheng and twenty other households and pardoned the rest of their followers.
translations.idiomatic: Daochan put Gongsheng and twenty other households to death and pardoned the remaining conspirators.

sentences.zh: 還為彭城王義康驃騎中兵參軍。

translations.literal: He returned to serve as Central Army Aide on the Flying Cavalry staff of Prince of Pengcheng Yikang.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned as central army aide on the Flying Cavalry staff of Prince of Pengcheng Liu Yikang.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三年，督梁、南秦二州諸軍事、寧遠將軍、西戎校尉、梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanjia he was made Supervisor of military affairs in Liang and Nanqin provinces, General of Distant Pacification, Colonel of the Western Rong, and Inspector of Liang and Nanqin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanjia (426) he was put in charge of military affairs in Liang and Nanqin, with the titles General of Distant Pacification, Colonel of the Western Rong, and inspector of both provinces.

sentences.zh: 在州有惠化，關中流民，前後出漢川歸之者甚多。

translations.literal: In his province he showed benevolent governance; many displaced people from Guanzhong came out through the Han valley to submit to him.
translations.idiomatic: His benevolent rule in the province drew many refugees from Guanzhong, who came through the Han valley to submit in large numbers.

sentences.zh: 六年，道產表置隴西、宋康二郡以領之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Daochan memorialized to establish the two commanderies of Longxi and Songkang to administer them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (429) Daochan petitioned to establish Longxi and Songkang commanderies to govern these settlers.

sentences.zh: 七年，徵為後軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was summoned to serve as General of the Rear Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (430) he was recalled to the capital as General of the Rear Guard.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷竟陵王義宣左將軍諮議參軍，仍為持節、督雍、梁、南秦三州、荊州之南陽、竟陵、順陽、襄陽、新野、隨六郡諸軍事、寧遠將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史、襄陽太守。

translations.literal: The following year he was transferred to consulting aide to the Left General under Prince of Jingling Yixuan, and at the same time made Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of military affairs in Yong, Liang, and Nanqin and six commanderies of Jing Province, General of Distant Pacification, Colonel Who Pacifies the Man, Inspector of Yong Province, and Administrator of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became consulting aide to the Left General on Prince of Jingling Liu Yixuan's staff, while also receiving the staff, supervision over Yong, Liang, and Nanqin and six Jing commanderies, the titles General of Distant Pacification and Colonel Who Pacifies the Man, the inspectorship of Yong, and the administration of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 善於臨民，在雍部政績尤著，蠻夷前後叛戾不受化者，竝皆順服，悉出緣沔為居。

translations.literal: Skilled in governing the people, he achieved especially notable results in Yong; barbarians who had repeatedly rebelled and refused civilization all submitted, and all moved out to settle along the Han.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at governing the people, he achieved his greatest record in Yong: tribes that had long defied assimilation all submitted and settled along the Han River.

sentences.zh: 百姓樂業，民戶豐贍，由此有《襄陽樂歌》，自道產始也。

translations.literal: The common people prospered in their occupations and households grew wealthy; from this arose the "Xiangyang Songs of Joy," which began with Daochan.
translations.idiomatic: The people prospered and households grew wealthy; from this came the "Xiangyang Songs of Joy," a tradition that began with Daochan.

sentences.zh: 十三年，進號輔國將軍。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year his title was advanced to General Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year (436) he was promoted to General Who Supports the State.

sentences.zh: 十九年卒，追贈征虜將軍，諡曰襄侯。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he died; posthumously he was given General Who Punishes the Barbarians, with the posthumous title Marquis of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the nineteenth year (442) and was posthumously honored as General Who Punishes the Barbarians, with the posthumous title Marquis of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 道產惠澤被於西土，及喪還，諸蠻皆備衰絰，號哭追送，至於沔口。

translations.literal: Daochan's benevolence had spread through the western lands; when his coffin returned, all the tribes put on mourning dress, wailed, and escorted him as far as the mouth of the Han.
translations.idiomatic: Daochan's kindness had spread through the west; when his funeral procession returned, the tribes all donned mourning, wailed, and escorted him to the mouth of the Han.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史衡陽王義季啟太祖曰：「故輔國將軍劉道產患背癰，疾遂不救。

translations.literal: Jing Inspector Prince of Hengyang Yiji memorialized the Emperor: "The late General Who Supports the State Liu Daochan suffered a carbuncle on his back; the illness proved fatal.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Inspector Prince of Hengyang Liu Yiji reported to the Emperor: "The late General Who Supports the State Liu Daochan developed a carbuncle on his back and could not be saved.

sentences.zh: 道產自鎮漢南，境接凶寇，政績既著，威懷兼舉。

translations.literal: Since Daochan garrisoned the south of the Han, his territory bordered fierce enemies; his administrative achievements were outstanding, and he combined authority with kindness.
translations.idiomatic: From his post south of the Han, on a frontier facing fierce enemies, he achieved outstanding administration, combining firm authority with humane governance.

sentences.zh: 年時猶可，方宣其用，奄至殞沒，傷怨特深。

translations.literal: His years were still fit; he was just coming into his full use when he suddenly perished—a loss felt with especial grief.
translations.idiomatic: He was still in his prime and ready for greater service when he died so suddenly; the grief at his loss is especially deep.

sentences.zh: 伏惟聖懷，愍惜兼至。」

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Sacred Heart feels both pity and regret to the fullest."
translations.idiomatic: I trust Your Majesty's heart feels the fullest pity and regret."

sentences.zh: 長子延孫，別有傳。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yansun has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yansun is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 延孫弟延熙，因延孫之廕，大明中，為司徒右長史，黃門郎，臨海、義興太守。

translations.literal: Yansun's younger brother Yanxi, through Yansun's hereditary privilege, in the Daming era served as Right Chief Clerk to the Minister over the Masses, Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, and Administrator of Linhai and Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Yansun's younger brother Yanxi, benefiting from Yansun's privilege, served in the Daming era as right chief clerk to the Minister over the Masses, gentleman at the Yellow Gate, and administrator of Linhai and Yixing.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，與四方同反，伏誅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he joined the rebellions in all quarters and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Taishi (465) he joined the widespread rebellions and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 道產弟道錫，巴西、梓潼二郡太守。

translations.literal: Daochan's younger brother Daoxi was Administrator of the two commanderies of Baxi and Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: Daochan's younger brother Daoxi served as administrator of Baxi and Zitong.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十八年，為氐寇所攻，道錫保城退敵，太祖嘉之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Yuanjia he was attacked by Di raiders; Daoxi held the city and repelled the enemy, and the Emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Yuanjia (441) Di raiders attacked him; Daoxi held the city and drove them off, winning the Emperor's praise.

sentences.zh: 下詔曰：「前者兵寇攻逼，邊情波駭，廣威將軍、巴西、梓潼二郡太守劉道錫，將率文武，盡心固守，保全之績，厥效可書。

translations.literal: An edict said: "When the army raiders pressed the attack and the frontier was in turmoil, General of Broad Prestige and Administrator of Baxi and Zitong Liu Daoxi led civil and military officials in devoted defense; his achievement in preserving the city is worthy of record.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "When raiders pressed the frontier and the border was in turmoil, General of Broad Prestige Liu Daoxi, administrator of Baxi and Zitong, led his officials in a resolute defense; his success in holding the city deserves to be recorded.

sentences.zh: 可冠軍。

translations.literal: He may be made Champion.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be promoted to Champion General.

sentences.zh: 諮議參軍、前建威將軍、晉壽太守申坦，孤城弱眾，厲志致果，死傷參半，壯氣不衰，雖力屈陷沒，在誠宜甄。

translations.literal: Consulting aide Shen Tan, former General Who Establishes Prestige and Administrator of Jinshou, with a lone city and weak forces, resolved his will to achieve results; casualties were half his men yet his spirit did not flag; though strength failed and the place fell, his loyalty deserves recognition.
translations.idiomatic: Consulting aide Shen Tan, former General Who Establishes Prestige and administrator of Jinshou, held a lone city with few troops, yet fought with fierce resolve; though half his men fell and the city was lost, his steadfast loyalty deserves reward.

sentences.zh: 可建威將軍、巴西、梓潼二郡太守。」

translations.literal: He may be made General Who Establishes Prestige and Administrator of Baxi and Zitong."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be made General Who Establishes Prestige and administrator of Baxi and Zitong."

sentences.zh: 初，氐寇至，城內眾寡，道錫募吏民守城，復租布二十年。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Di raiders arrived and forces in the city were few, Daoxi recruited officials and people to defend the walls and remitted rent and cloth taxes for twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: When the Di raiders first came and the garrison was weak, Daoxi recruited officials and commoners to defend the walls and promised a twenty-year remission of rent and cloth taxes.

sentences.zh: 及賊退，朝議：「賊雖攻城，一戰便走，聽依本要，於事為優。」

translations.literal: When the raiders withdrew, the court debated: "Though the raiders besieged the city, they fled after one battle; to follow the original promise would be best for the matter."
translations.idiomatic: After the raiders withdrew, the court debated: "Though the raiders besieged the city, they fled after one battle; to follow the original promise would be best for the matter."

sentences.zh: 右衛將軍沈演之、丹陽尹羊玄保、後軍長史范曄竝謂：「宜隨功勞裁量，不可全用本誓，多者不得過十年。」

translations.literal: Right Guard General Shen Yanzhi, Governor of Danyang Yang Xuanbao, and Chief Clerk of the Rear Guard Fan Ye all said: "The remission should be scaled to merit; the original pledge cannot be applied in full—at most ten years."
translations.idiomatic: Right Guard General Shen Yanzhi, governor of Danyang Yang Xuanbao, and chief clerk of the rear guard Fan Ye all said: "The remission should be scaled to merit; the original pledge cannot be applied in full—at most ten years."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted their view.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，遷揚烈將軍、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to General Who Raises the Host and Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year (444) he was transferred to General Who Raises the Host and inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，坐貪縱過度，自杖治中荀齊文垂死，乘輿出城行，與阿尼同載，為有司所糾。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was charged with excessive greed and indulgence: he personally beat Chief Clerk Xun Qiwen nearly to death, rode out of the city in the imperial carriage, and shared a carriage with a Buddhist nun; the authorities impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year (450) he was impeached for gross corruption and license: he had personally beaten chief clerk Xun Qiwen nearly to death, rode out in the official carriage, and shared it with a Buddhist nun.

sentences.zh: 值赦，明年散徵。

translations.literal: An amnesty intervened; the following year he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty spared him; the next year he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 又以赦後餘贓，收下廷尉，被宥病卒。

translations.literal: Again, for remaining offenses after the amnesty, he was handed to the Court of Justice, pardoned, and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was again tried for offenses remaining after the amnesty, handed to the Court of Justice, pardoned, and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 杜驥，字度世，京兆杜陵人也。

translations.literal: Du Ji, style name Dushi, was a native of Duling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ji, whose courtesy name was Dushi, came from Duling in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 高祖預，晉征南將軍。

translations.literal: His ancestor Yu was Jin General of the South.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Yu served Jin as General of the South.

sentences.zh: 曾祖耽，避難河西，因仕張氏。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Dan fled to Hexi for refuge and entered the service of the Zhang clan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Dan took refuge in Hexi and entered the service of the Zhang regime.

sentences.zh: 苻堅平涼州，父祖始還關中。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian pacified Liang Province, his father and grandfather returned to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian pacified Liang Province, his father and grandfather returned to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 兄坦，頗涉史傳。

translations.literal: His elder brother Tan was well versed in historical writings.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Tan was well read in history.

sentences.zh: 高祖征長安，席捲隨從南還。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor campaigned against Chang'an, he swept along in the train and returned south.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor campaigned against Chang'an, he joined the southward march and returned with the army.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉中，任遇甚厚，歷後軍將軍，龍驤將軍，青、冀二州刺史，南平王鑠右將軍司馬。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era under Emperor Wen, Tan received very generous appointments, serving as General of the Rear Guard, General of the Soaring Dragon, Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, and Chief of Staff to the Right General under Prince of Nanping Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen in the Yuanjia era Tan enjoyed exceptional favor, serving as rear guard general, soaring dragon general, inspector of Qing and Ji, and chief of staff to Prince of Nanping Liu Shuo's right general.

sentences.zh: 晚度北人，朝廷常以傖荒遇之，雖復人才可施，每為清塗所隔，坦以此慨然。

translations.literal: As a northerner who had crossed south late, the court always treated him as crude and rustic; though his talent could have been used, he was repeatedly blocked by the pure elite, and Tan lamented this.
translations.idiomatic: As a northerner who had crossed south late, the court treated him as an outsider; though his talent was usable, the established elite kept him out, and Tan brooded bitterly over this.

sentences.zh: 嘗與太祖言及史籍，上曰：「金日磾忠孝淳深，漢朝莫及，恨今世無復如此輩人。」

translations.literal: Once when speaking with the Emperor about historical records, the Emperor said: "Jin Midi's loyalty and filial piety were pure and deep; the Han could not match him—I regret that our age has no such men."
translations.idiomatic: Once, discussing history with the Emperor, the Emperor said, "Jin Midi's loyalty and filial devotion were profound beyond anything in Han times—I regret that men like him no longer exist today."

sentences.zh: 坦曰：「日磾之美，誠如聖詔。

translations.literal: Tan said: "Midi's excellence is indeed as Your Sacred Edict states.
translations.idiomatic: Tan replied, "Midi's excellence is indeed as Your Majesty says.

sentences.zh: 假使生乎今世，養馬不暇，豈辦見知。」

translations.literal: Had he been born in our age, he would have had no leisure beyond tending horses—how could he have won recognition?"
translations.idiomatic: Had he lived in our age, he would have had no time beyond tending horses—how could he ever have been noticed?"

sentences.zh: 上變色曰：「卿何量朝廷之薄也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor changed color and said: "Why do you measure the court so meanly?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's face darkened. "Why do you think so little of the court?"

sentences.zh: 坦曰：「請以臣言之。

translations.literal: Tan said: "Allow me to speak from my own case.
translations.idiomatic: Tan said, "Let me speak from my own case.

sentences.zh: 臣本中華高族，亡曾祖晉氏喪亂，播遷涼土，世葉相承，不殞其舊。

translations.literal: I am originally of a lofty Chinese clan; my late great-grandfather, in Jin's turmoil, was scattered to Liang territory, yet generation after generation preserved our old standing.
translations.idiomatic: I come from a distinguished Chinese house; my great-grandfather was driven to Liang in Jin's collapse, yet our line preserved its standing generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 直以南度不早，便以荒傖賜隔。

translations.literal: Simply because we crossed south too late, we are set apart as crude outsiders.
translations.idiomatic: Simply because we crossed south too late, we are dismissed as crude outsiders.

sentences.zh: 日磾胡人，身為牧圉，便超入內侍，齒列名賢。

translations.literal: Midi was a barbarian who tended horses, yet he rose at once to inner attendance and stood among the famed worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Midi was a foreigner who tended horses, yet he rose straight into the inner court and stood among the great men of his age.

sentences.zh: 聖朝雖復拔才，臣恐未必能也。」

translations.literal: Though our sage dynasty may also promote talent, I fear it could not do the same."
translations.idiomatic: Though our sage dynasty may promote talent, I doubt it could do the same today."

sentences.zh: 上默然。

translations.literal: The Emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 北土舊法，問疾必遣子弟。

translations.literal: By northern custom, when inquiring after the sick one must send one's sons or younger kin.
translations.idiomatic: In the north it was customary to send one's sons when inquiring after the sick.

sentences.zh: 驥年十三，父使候同郡韋華。

translations.literal: Ji was thirteen when his father sent him to call on Wei Hua of the same commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji was thirteen, his father sent him to inquire after Wei Hua of the same commandery.

sentences.zh: 華子玄有高名，見而異之，以女妻焉。

translations.literal: Hua's son Xuan had a high reputation; seeing Ji he was struck by him and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Hua's son Xuan was highly regarded; struck by Ji at their meeting, he gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 桂陽公義真鎮長安，辟為州主簿，後為義真車騎行參軍，員外散騎侍郎，江夏王義恭撫軍刑獄參軍，尚書都官郎，長沙王義欣後軍錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When Duke of Guiyang Yizhen garrisoned Chang'an, Ji was recruited as provincial chief clerk; later he served Yizhen as acting aide on the Chariots and Cavalry staff, External Gentleman Attendant-at-Court, aide for punishments on Prince of Jiangxia Yigong's Pacification Army staff, Director in the Ministry of Justice, and recording aide on Prince of Changsha Yixin's Rear Guard staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Guiyang Liu Yizhen held Chang'an, Ji was recruited as provincial chief clerk; he later served as acting aide on Yizhen's chariots and cavalry staff, external attendant gentleman, punishments aide on Prince of Jiangxia Liu Yigong's pacification army staff, director in the Ministry of Justice, and recording aide on Prince of Changsha Liu Yixin's rear guard staff.

sentences.zh: 元嘉七年，隨到彥之入河南，加建武將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanjia he followed Dao Yanzhi into Henan and was given the additional title General Who Establishes Martial Prestige.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yuanjia (430) he followed Dao Yanzhi into Henan and was made General Who Establishes Martial Prestige.

sentences.zh: 索虜撤河南戍悉歸河北，彥之使驥守洛陽。

translations.literal: The Northern Wei withdrew all Henan garrisons north of the river; Yanzhi ordered Ji to hold Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei pulled all Henan garrisons back north of the river, and Yanzhi left Ji to hold Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 洛陽城不治既久，又無糧食，及彥之敗退，驥欲棄城走，慮為太祖所誅。

translations.literal: Luoyang had long gone unrepaired and had no provisions; when Yanzhi was defeated and withdrew, Ji wished to abandon the city and flee but feared execution by the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang had long been neglected and had no grain; when Yanzhi was routed, Ji wanted to abandon the city and flee but feared the Emperor would have him executed.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖平關洛，致鐘虡舊器南還，一大鐘墜洛水。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Founding Emperor pacified Guan and Luo, he sent the old bells and ritual vessels south; one great bell fell into the Luo River.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor had pacified Guan and Luo, he sent the ancient bells and vessels south; one great bell had fallen into the Luo River.

sentences.zh: 至是太祖遣將姚聳夫領千五百人迎致之。

translations.literal: Now the Emperor sent the general Yao Songfu with fifteen hundred men to bring it back.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor now sent General Yao Songfu with fifteen hundred men to recover it.

sentences.zh: 時聳夫政率所領牽鐘于洛水，驥乃誑之曰：「虜既南渡，洛城勢弱，今修理城池，竝已堅固，軍糧又足，所乏者人耳。

translations.literal: At that time Songfu was just leading his men to haul the bell at the Luo; Ji deceived him, saying: "The barbarians have crossed south and Luoyang is weak—but we have now repaired the walls and they are firm, provisions are ample, and all we lack is men.
translations.idiomatic: Songfu was then hauling the bell at the Luo when Ji deceived him: "The enemy has crossed south and Luoyang looks weak—but we have repaired the walls, provisions are ample, and we only lack men.

sentences.zh: 君率眾見就，共守此城，大功既立，取鐘無晚。」

translations.literal: Lead your men here and defend this city with us; once the great achievement is won, retrieving the bell will not be late."
translations.idiomatic: Bring your men and help hold the city; once we have done that, there will be time enough to fetch the bell."

sentences.zh: 聳夫信之，率所領就驥。

translations.literal: Songfu believed him and led his men to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Songfu believed him and led his men to Ji.

sentences.zh: 既至，見城不可守，又無糧食，於是引眾去。

translations.literal: When they arrived and saw the city could not be held and there was no food, they led their men away.
translations.idiomatic: Once there, they saw the city could not be held and there was no food, and they led their men away.

sentences.zh: 驥亦委城南奔，白太祖曰：「本欲以死固守，姚聳夫及城便走，人情沮敗，不可復禁。」

translations.literal: Ji too abandoned the city and fled south, reporting to the Emperor: "I had meant to hold firm unto death, but when Yao Songfu reached the city he fled at once; morale collapsed and could not be restrained."
translations.idiomatic: Ji too abandoned the city and fled south, reporting to the Emperor: "I had meant to die defending it, but when Yao Songfu arrived he fled at once; morale collapsed and could not be held."

sentences.zh: 上大怒，使建威將軍鄭順之殺聳夫於壽陽。

translations.literal: The Emperor was furious and sent General Who Establishes Prestige Zheng Shunzhi to execute Songfu at Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious and sent General Who Establishes Prestige Zheng Shunzhi to execute Songfu at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 聳夫，吳興武康人。

translations.literal: Songfu was a man of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Songfu was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 勇果有氣力，宋世偏裨小將莫及。

translations.literal: Brave, resolute, and strong, no subordinate general of the Song could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Brave, fierce, and immensely strong, no subordinate general of the Song could match him.

sentences.zh: 始隨到彥之北伐，與虜遇，聳夫手斬托跋燾叔父英文特勒首，燾以馬百匹贖之。

translations.literal: At first he followed Dao Yanzhi on the northern campaign; meeting the enemy, Songfu personally beheaded Tuoba Tao's uncle Yingwen Tele; Tao ransomed the head with a hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: He had first followed Dao Yanzhi north; in battle he personally beheaded Tuoba Tao's uncle Yingwen Tele, and Tao ransomed the head with a hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 以驥為通直郎，射聲校尉，世祖征虜諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Ji was made Direct Attendant, Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound, and consulting aide on the future Emperor Xiaowu's staff as Vanquisher of Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was made direct attendant, colonel of the archers who shoot at sound, and consulting aide on the future Emperor Xiaowu's staff as Vanquisher of Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 十七年，出督青、冀二州、徐州之東莞、東安二郡諸軍事、寧遠將軍、青、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he went out to supervise military affairs in Qing and Ji provinces and the two Xu commanderies of Dongguan and Dong'an, as General of Distant Pacification and Inspector of Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year (440) he was sent out to supervise military affairs in Qing and Ji and in Dongguan and Dong'an of Xu, as General of Distant Pacification and inspector of Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 在任八年，惠化著於齊土。

translations.literal: In eight years in office his benevolent governance was renowned throughout Qi territory.
translations.idiomatic: In eight years in office his benevolent rule became renowned throughout Qi.

sentences.zh: 自義熙至於宋末，刺史唯羊穆之及驥，為吏民所稱詠。

translations.literal: From Yixi to the end of Song, only Yang Muzhi and Ji among inspectors were praised and celebrated by officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: From Yixi to the end of Song, only Yang Muzhi and Ji among provincial inspectors won lasting praise from officials and people alike.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，徵左軍將軍，兄坦代為刺史，北土以為榮焉。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was summoned as General of the Left Army; his elder brother Tan replaced him as inspector, and northerners took this as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year (447) he was recalled as General of the Left Army; his elder brother Tan took over as inspector, which northerners regarded as a great honor.

sentences.zh: 坦長子琬為員外散騎侍郎，太祖嘗有函詔敕坦，琬輒開視。

translations.literal: Tan's eldest son Wan was External Gentleman Attendant-at-Court; the Emperor once had a sealed edict for Tan, and Wan opened and read it.
translations.idiomatic: Tan's eldest son Wan served as external attendant gentleman; once the Emperor sent Tan a sealed edict, and Wan opened and read it.

sentences.zh: 信未發又追取之，敕函已發，大相推檢。

translations.literal: Before the letter was sent it was recalled; since the sealed edict had been opened, a major investigation followed.
translations.idiomatic: Before the messenger departed the letter was recalled; because the seal had been broken, a major investigation ensued.

sentences.zh: 丞都答云：「諸郎開視。」

translations.literal: The chief clerk of the prefecture answered: "The young gentlemen opened and read it."
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural chief clerk replied, "The young gentlemen opened it."

sentences.zh: 上遣主書詰責，驥答曰：「開函是臣第四子季文，伏待刑坐。」

translations.literal: The Emperor sent a chief clerk to question and rebuke him; Ji answered: "The one who opened the seal was my fourth son Jiwen; I submit myself to punishment."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent a chief clerk to investigate; Ji answered, "My fourth son Jiwen opened the seal; I await punishment."

sentences.zh: 上特原不問。

translations.literal: The Emperor specially pardoned him and took no further action.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor specially pardoned him and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，卒，時年六十四。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he died, at the age of sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-seventh year (450), at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 長子長文，早卒。

translations.literal: His eldest son Changwen died young.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Changwen died young.

sentences.zh: 第五子幼文，薄於行。

translations.literal: His fifth son Youwen was deficient in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth son Youwen was morally deficient.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，以軍功為驍騎將軍，封邵陽縣男，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign, for military merit he was made General of Valiant Cavalry, enfeoffed as Baron of Shaoyang County with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Ming's reign he was made General of Valiant Cavalry for military merit and enfeoffed as Baron of Shaoyang with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋坐巧佞奪爵。

translations.literal: Soon he was stripped of his rank for crafty flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he lost his title for crafty sycophancy.

sentences.zh: 後以發太尉廬江王禕謀反事，拜黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Later, for exposing the rebellion plot of Grand Marshal Prince of Lujiang Yi, he was made Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for exposing Grand Marshal Prince of Lujiang Liu Yi's rebellion, he was made gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 出為輔國將軍、梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Supports the State and Inspector of Liang and Nanqin provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Supports the State and inspector of Liang and Nanqin.

sentences.zh: 廢帝元徽中，為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Under the Deposed Emperor in the Yuanhui era he served as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Deposed Emperor in the Yuanhui era he served as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 幼文所蒞貪橫，家累千金，女伎數十人，絲竹晝夜不絕，與沈勃、孫超之居止接近，常相從，又竝與阮佃夫厚善。

translations.literal: In every post Youwen was greedy and overbearing; his household amassed thousands in gold; he kept dozens of female performers and music sounded day and night; he lived near Shen Bo and Sun Chaozhi and constantly kept their company; he was also on close terms with Ruan Dianfu.
translations.idiomatic: In every office Youwen was greedy and domineering; his household amassed great wealth; he kept dozens of female performers and music never ceased day or night; he lived near Shen Bo and Sun Chaozhi and kept their company constantly; he was also intimate with Ruan Dianfu.

sentences.zh: 佃夫死，廢帝深疾之。

translations.literal: When Dianfu died, the Deposed Emperor deeply resented them.
translations.idiomatic: After Dianfu's death, the Deposed Emperor came to hate them deeply.

sentences.zh: 帝微行夜出，輒在幼文門牆之間，聽其弦管，積久轉不能平，於是自率宿衛兵誅幼文、勃、超之等。

translations.literal: The Emperor would go out incognito at night and linger by Youwen's gate to listen to his strings and pipes; over time his resentment could not be appeased, and he personally led the palace guard to execute Youwen, Bo, Chaozhi, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would slip out at night and linger by Youwen's gate listening to his music; as his resentment mounted he personally led the palace guard to execute Youwen, Bo, Chaozhi, and the others.

sentences.zh: 幼文兄叔文為長水校尉，及諸子侄在京邑方鎮者竝誅。

translations.literal: Youwen's elder brother Shuwen was Colonel of the Long River; all sons and nephews in the capital or in provincial posts were likewise executed.
translations.idiomatic: Youwen's elder brother Shuwen was colonel of the Long River; all his sons and nephews in the capital or in the provinces were executed as well.

sentences.zh: 唯幼文兄季文、弟希文等數人，逃亡得免。

translations.literal: Only Youwen's elder brother Jiwen, younger brother Xiwen, and a few others escaped by flight.
translations.idiomatic: Only Youwen's elder brother Jiwen, younger brother Xiwen, and a few others escaped by fleeing.

sentences.zh: 申恬，字公休，魏郡魏人也。

translations.literal: Shen Tian, style name Gongxiu, was a native of Wei in Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tian, whose courtesy name was Gongxiu, came from Wei in Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖鍾，為石虎司徒。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zhong served Shi Hu as Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zhong served Shi Hu as Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 高祖平廣固，恬父宣、宣從父兄永皆得歸國，竝以幹用見知。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor pacified Guanggu, Tian's father Xuan and Xuan's cousin Yong were both able to return to the realm and were known for practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor pacified Guanggu, Tian's father Xuan and Xuan's cousin Yong both returned to Song and were valued for their practical ability.

sentences.zh: 永歷青、兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: Yong served as Inspector of Qing and Yan provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Yong served as inspector of Qing and Yan.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐祚，拜太中大夫。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor took the throne, Yong was made Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor took the throne, Yong was made grand master of palace counsel.

sentences.zh: 宣，太祖元嘉初，亦歷兗、青二州刺史。

translations.literal: Xuan, at the beginning of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, also served as Inspector of Yan and Qing provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, at the start of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, also served as inspector of Yan and Qing.

sentences.zh: 恬兄謨，與朱脩之守滑臺，為虜所沒，後得叛還。

translations.literal: Tian's elder brother Mo, with Zhu Xiuzhi, held Huatai; he was captured by the enemy but later defected back.
translations.idiomatic: Tian's elder brother Mo held Huatai with Zhu Xiuzhi, was captured by the enemy, and later defected back.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，為竟陵太守。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era he served as Administrator of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanjia era he served as administrator of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 恬初為驃騎道憐長兼行參軍。

translations.literal: Tian first served as senior acting aide on Daolian's Flying Cavalry staff.
translations.idiomatic: Tian first served as senior acting aide on Liu Daolian's Flying Cavalry staff.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐祚，拜東宮殿中將軍，度還臺。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor took the throne, Tian was made Palace General of the Eastern Palace and then transferred back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor took the throne, Tian was made palace general of the Eastern Palace and then returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 直省十載，不請休息。

translations.literal: For ten years on palace duty he never asked for leave.
translations.idiomatic: For ten years on palace duty he never asked for a rest.

sentences.zh: 轉員外散騎侍郎，出為綏遠將軍、下邳太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to External Gentleman Attendant-at-Court, then went out as General Who Pacifies the Distance and Administrator of Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to external attendant gentleman, then sent out as General Who Pacifies the Distance and administrator of Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 轉在北海，加寧遠將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Beihai and given the additional title General of Distant Pacification.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Beihai and given the additional title General of Distant Pacification.

sentences.zh: 所至皆有政績。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he achieved administrative results.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he left a record of good administration.

sentences.zh: 又為北譙、梁二郡太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He also served as Administrator of the two commanderies of Beiqiao and Liang, his general's rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as administrator of Beiqiao and Liang, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 郡境邊接任榛，屢被寇抄。

translations.literal: The commandery bordered Renzhen and was repeatedly raided.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery bordered Renzhen and suffered repeated raids.

sentences.zh: 恬到，密知賊來，仍伏兵要害，出其不意，悉皆禽殄。

translations.literal: When Tian arrived he secretly learned the raiders were coming, set ambush at a critical point, took them by surprise, and captured or killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian arrived he learned secretly that raiders were coming, laid ambush at a choke point, surprised them, and captured or killed them all.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十二年，遷督魯、東平、濟北三郡軍事、泰山太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to supervise military affairs in the three commanderies of Lu, Dongping, and Jibei, and Administrator of Taishan, his general's rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia (435) he was put in charge of military affairs in Lu, Dongping, and Jibei and made administrator of Taishan, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 惠威兼著，吏民便之。

translations.literal: His kindness and authority were both manifest; officials and people found him a benefit.
translations.idiomatic: His kindness and authority were both evident, and officials and people prospered under him.

sentences.zh: 臨川王義慶鎮江陵，為平西中兵參軍、河東太守。

translations.literal: When Prince of Linchuan Yiqing garrisoned Jiangling, Tian served as Central Army Aide on the Pacify-the-West staff and Administrator of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Linchuan Liu Yiqing held Jiangling, Tian served as central army aide on the pacify-the-west staff and administrator of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 衡陽王義季代義慶，又度安西府，加寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: When Prince of Hengyang Yiji replaced Yiqing, Tian was again transferred to the Pacify-the-West headquarters and given the additional title General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Hengyang Liu Yiji replaced Yiqing, Tian was transferred to the pacify-the-west headquarters and made General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 召拜太子屯騎校尉，母憂去職。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Colonel of the Heir's Garrison Cavalry, then left office for his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as colonel of the heir's garrison cavalry, then left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，冀州移鎮歷下，以恬督冀州、青州之濟南、樂安、太原三郡諸軍事、揚烈將軍、冀州刺史，明年，加濟南太守。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Jizhou's headquarters moved to Lixia; Tian was made Supervisor of military affairs in Jizhou and the three Qing commanderies of Jinan, Le'an, and Taiyuan, General Who Raises the Host, and Inspector of Jizhou; the following year he was also given Jinan as administrator.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year (444) Jizhou's seat moved to Lixia; Tian was put in charge of military affairs in Jizhou and in Jinan, Le'an, and Taiyuan of Qing, as General Who Raises the Host and inspector of Jizhou; the next year he was also made administrator of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 時又遷換諸郡守，恬上表曰：「伏聞朝恩當加臣濟南太守，仰惟優旨，荒心散越。

translations.literal: At that time commandery administrators were being rotated; Tian memorialized: "I humbly hear that the court's grace will add to me the administration of Jinan; looking up at this excellent decree, my confused heart is scattered beyond itself.
translations.idiomatic: As commandery administrators were being rotated, Tian memorialized: "I humbly hear that the court intends to add Jinan to my charge; at this gracious decree my bewildered heart is overwhelmed with gratitude.

sentences.zh: 臣殃咎之餘，遭蒙逾忝，寵私罔己，復兼今授，豈其愚迷，所能上答。

translations.literal: I am one who survives calamity and fault, yet have received favor beyond my deserts; private grace knows no limit, and now this added appointment—how could my foolish blindness repay it?
translations.idiomatic: I am one who survives disgrace and fault, yet have received favor beyond my deserts; your private grace knows no limit, and now this added appointment—how could my dull wits ever repay it?

sentences.zh: 臣近至止，即履行所統，究其形宜。

translations.literal: Since I recently arrived I have at once toured what I govern and examined its terrain and conditions.
translations.idiomatic: Since my recent arrival I have toured my jurisdiction and studied its terrain and conditions.

sentences.zh: 河、濟之間，應置戍捍，其中四處，急須修立，甕口故城，又是要所，宜移太原，委以邊事。

translations.literal: Between the Yellow and Ji rivers garrisons should be set; of these four sites urgently need rebuilding; the old city at Wengkou is again a critical point—Taiyuan should be moved there and entrusted with frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Yellow and Ji rivers garrisons are needed; four sites urgently require rebuilding; the old city at Wengkou is again critical—Taiyuan should be moved there and entrusted with frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 緣山諸邏，並得除省，防衛綏懷，利便非一。

translations.literal: The mountain guard posts could all be abolished; defense, pacification, and care would gain many advantages.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain guard posts could all be abolished, yielding many advantages in defense and pacification.

sentences.zh: 呂綽誠效益著，深同臣意，百姓聞者，咸皆附說，急有同異，二三未宜。

translations.literal: Lu Chuo's loyal service and benefits are clear and deeply accord with my view; common people who hear of it all endorse the plan—only two or three urgent points of disagreement remain unsuitable.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chuo's loyal service is evident and fully accords with my view; the people who hear of it all endorse the plan—only two or three urgent points still seem ill-advised.

sentences.zh: 但房紹之蒞郡經年，軍民粗狎，改以帶臣，有乖永事。

translations.literal: But Fang Shaozhi has governed the commandery for years and army and people are already familiar with him; to replace him with me in an additional post would harm long-term affairs.
translations.idiomatic: But Fang Shaozhi has governed the commandery for years and the army and people are already accustomed to him; replacing him with me in an added post would harm long-term stability.

sentences.zh: 遠牽太原，於民為苦。

translations.literal: Moving Taiyuan far away would be a hardship for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Moving Taiyuan far away would burden the people.

sentences.zh: 而甕口之計，復成交互，人情非樂，容有不安。

translations.literal: Moreover the Wengkou plan would again create cross-assignments; popular feeling would not be pleased and unrest might arise.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Wengkou plan would again shuffle assignments; the people would not welcome it and unrest might follow.

sentences.zh: 疆場威刑，患不開廣，若得依先處分，公私允緝。」

translations.literal: On the frontier authority and punishment fear not being broad enough; if the prior disposition can be followed, public and private interests will both be settled."
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier we fear authority will not reach far enough; if the prior arrangement can stand, public and private interests will both be secure."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 詔有司曰：「恬所陳當是事宜，近諸除授可悉停。」

translations.literal: An edict to the authorities said: "What Tian has stated fits the circumstances; all recent appointments may be halted entirely."
translations.idiomatic: An edict to the authorities said, "Tian's memorial fits the circumstances; halt all recent appointments."

sentences.zh: 北虜入寇，恬摧擊之，為虜所破，被徴還都。

translations.literal: When the northern barbarians invaded, Tian attacked and crushed them but was defeated by the enemy and was summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern barbarians invaded, Tian struck at them but was defeated and recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，起為通直常侍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was recalled to serve as Regular Attendant for Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year (450) he was recalled as regular attendant for direct communication.

sentences.zh: 是歲，索虜南寇，其武昌王向青州。

translations.literal: That year the Northern Wei invaded south; their Prince of Wuchang advanced on Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Northern Wei invaded south; their Prince of Wuchang advanced on Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 遣恬援東陽，因與輔國司馬、齊郡太守龐秀之保城固守。

translations.literal: Tian was sent to aid Dongyang and, with the State-Supporting Army's Chief of Staff and Administrator of Qi commandery Pang Xiuzhi, held the city in a firm defense.
translations.idiomatic: Tian was sent to relieve Dongyang and, with chief of staff Pang Xiuzhi of the state-supporting army and administrator of Qi commandery, held the city in a resolute defense.

sentences.zh: 蕭斌遣青州別駕解榮之率垣護之還援恬等，仍傍南山得入。

translations.literal: Xiao Bin sent Qing Provincial Attendant Xie Rongzhi leading Yuan Huzhi back to aid Tian and the others; they entered by way of the southern hills.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Bin sent Qing provincial attendant Xie Rongzhi with Yuan Huzhi to relieve Tian and the others; they entered along the southern hills.

sentences.zh: 賊朝來脅城，日晚輒退。

translations.literal: The enemy came each morning to threaten the city and withdrew each evening.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy came each morning to threaten the city and withdrew each evening.

sentences.zh: 城內乃出車北門外，環塹為營，欲挑戰，賊不敢逼。

translations.literal: Those inside then sent chariots out the north gate, ringed the moat with camps, and sought battle; the enemy did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders then sent chariots out the north gate, ringed the moat with camps, and offered battle; the enemy did not dare close in.

sentences.zh: 停五日，東過抄略清河郡及驛道南數千家，從東安、東莞出下邳。

translations.literal: After five days' halt they passed east, raiding Qinghe commandery and several thousand households south of the post road, and left through Dong'an and Dongguan for Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: After five days they moved east, raiding Qinghe commandery and thousands of households south of the post road, then passed through Dong'an and Dongguan toward Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 下邳太守垣閬閉城距守，保全二千餘家。

translations.literal: Xiapi Administrator Yuan Lang closed the city and resisted, preserving more than two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Xiapi administrator Yuan Lang shut the city and held out, saving more than two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 虜退，以恬為寧朔將軍、山陽太守。

translations.literal: When the barbarians withdrew, Tian was made General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the invaders withdrew, Tian was made General Who Pacifies the North and administrator of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 善於治民，所蒞有績。

translations.literal: Skilled in governing the people, he achieved results in every post.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at governing the people, he achieved results in every office he held.

sentences.zh: 世祖踐阼，遷青州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: When the Heir ascended the throne, Tian was transferred to Inspector of Qing Province, his general's rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, Tian was transferred to inspector of Qing Province, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 尋加督徐州之東莞、東安二郡諸軍事。

translations.literal: Soon he was also given supervision of military affairs in the two Xu commanderies of Dongguan and Dong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also put in charge of military affairs in Dongguan and Dong'an of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 明年，又督冀州。

translations.literal: The following year he was also given supervision of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was also put in charge of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 齊地連歲興兵，百姓凋弊，恬初防衛邊境，勸課農桑，二三年間，遂皆優實。

translations.literal: Qi territory had seen war year after year and the people were depleted; when Tian first defended the frontier he urged agriculture and sericulture, and within two or three years all became prosperous and secure.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had suffered years of war and the people were exhausted; when Tian first took up frontier defense he promoted farming and sericulture, and within two or three years the region prospered again.

sentences.zh: 性清約，頻處州郡，妻子不免饑寒，世以此稱之。

translations.literal: By nature he was austere and frugal; though he often held provincial posts, his wife and children did not escape hunger and cold—the age praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was austere; though he often held high provincial office, his wife and children still knew hunger and cold—and the age praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 進號輔國將軍。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to General Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Supports the State.

sentences.zh: 孝建二年，遷督豫州軍事、寧朔將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian he was transferred to supervise military affairs in Yuzhou, as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiaojian (455) he was put in charge of military affairs in Yuzhou as General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，疾病徵還，於道卒，時年六十九。

translations.literal: The following year, ill, he was summoned back and died on the road at the age of sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, recalled while ill, he died on the road at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 死之日，家無遺財。

translations.literal: On the day of his death his household had no property left.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he died his household had no property left.

sentences.zh: 子實，南譙郡太守，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Shi was Administrator of Nanqiao commandery and died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi, administrator of Nanqiao commandery, died young.

sentences.zh: 謨子元嗣，海陵、廣陵太守。

translations.literal: Mo's son Yuansi was Administrator of Hailing and Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Mo's son Yuansi served as administrator of Hailing and Guangling.

sentences.zh: 元嗣弟謙，太始初，以軍功歷軍校，官至輔國將軍、臨川內史。

translations.literal: Yuansi's younger brother Qian, at the beginning of Taishi, for military merit rose through army commands to General Who Supports the State and Interior Administrator of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansi's younger brother Qian, at the start of Taishi, rose through military ranks for merit to General Who Supports the State and interior administrator of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 永子坦，自巴西、梓潼遷梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: Yong's son Tan was transferred from Baxi and Zitong to Inspector of Liang and Nanqin provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's son Tan was transferred from Baxi and Zitong to inspector of Liang and Nanqin.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十六年，為世祖鎮軍諮議參軍，與王玄謨圍滑臺不克，免官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia he was consulting aide on the Pacification Army staff under the Heir; with Wang Xuanmo he besieged Huatai without success and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia (449) he was consulting aide on the heir's pacification army staff; he joined Wang Xuanmo in besieging Huatai without success and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史蕭斌板行建威將軍、濟南、平原二郡太守，復攻確磝，敗退，下歷城。

translations.literal: Qing Inspector Xiao Bin appointed him acting General Who Establishes Prestige and Administrator of Jinan and Pingyuan; he again attacked Que'ao, was defeated and withdrew, and went down to Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qing inspector Xiao Bin appointed him acting General Who Establishes Prestige and administrator of Jinan and Pingyuan; he attacked Que'ao again, was routed, and withdrew to Licheng.

sentences.zh: 蕭思話起義討元兇，假坦輔國將軍，為前鋒。

translations.literal: When Xiao Sihua raised forces to punish the usurper, Tan was provisionally made General Who Supports the State and served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Sihua rose to punish the usurper, Tan was provisionally made General Who Supports the State and led the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 世祖至新亭，坦亦進克京城。

translations.literal: When the Heir reached Xinting, Tan also advanced and captured the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir reached Xinting, Tan also advanced and captured the capital.

sentences.zh: 孝建初，為太子右衛率，寧朔將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojian he was Right Commandant of the Heir's Guard, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xiaojian he was right commandant of the heir's guard, General Who Pacifies the North, and inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 大明元年，虜寇兗州，世祖遣太子衛率薛安都、新除東陽太守沈法系北討，至兗州，虜已去。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daming the barbarians raided Yanzhou; Emperor Xiaowu sent Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard Xue Andu and the newly appointed Administrator of Dongyang Shen Faxing north to attack; when they reached Yanzhou the enemy had already gone.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daming (457) the barbarians raided Yanzhou; Emperor Xiaowu sent Xue Andu, commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard, and the newly appointed Dongyang administrator Shen Faxing north; by the time they reached Yanzhou the enemy was gone.

sentences.zh: 坦建議：「任榛亡命，屢犯邊民，軍出無功，宜因此翦撲。」

translations.literal: Tan proposed: "The outlaws of Renzhen have repeatedly harmed border people; the campaign achieved nothing—we should use this opportunity to destroy them."
translations.idiomatic: Tan proposed: "The Renzhen outlaws have repeatedly raided the border; the campaign achieved nothing—we should use this chance to wipe them out."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 亡命先已聞知，舉村逃走，安都與法系坐白衣領職，坦棄市。

translations.literal: The outlaws had already heard and whole villages fled; Andu and Faxing were reduced to commoners retaining office, and Tan was executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: The outlaws had already heard and whole villages fled; Andu and Faxing were demoted to commoners while retaining office, and Tan was executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 群臣為之請，莫能得。

translations.literal: The ministers pleaded for him but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers pleaded for him in vain.

sentences.zh: 將行刑，始興公沈慶之入市抱坦慟哭曰：「卿無罪，為朝廷所枉誅，我入市亦當不久。」

translations.literal: As execution was about to take place, Duke of Shixing Shen Qingzhi entered the market, embraced Tan, and wept aloud: "You are guiltless, wrongly killed by the court—I too shall enter the market before long."
translations.idiomatic: As execution neared, Duke of Shixing Shen Qingzhi entered the market, embraced Tan, and wept: "You are innocent, wrongly killed by the court—I too shall soon enter this market."

sentences.zh: 市官以白上，乃原生命，繫尚方。

translations.literal: The market official reported this to the Emperor, who then spared his life and imprisoned him in the Imperial Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: The market official reported this to the emperor, who spared Tan's life and imprisoned him in the Imperial Workshops.

sentences.zh: 尋被宥，復為驍騎將軍，病卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was pardoned, restored as General of Valiant Cavalry, and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon pardoned, he was restored as General of Valiant Cavalry and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 子令孫，前廢帝景和中，為永嘉王子仁左軍司馬、廣陵太守。

translations.literal: His son Lingsun, in the Jinghe era under the Former Deposed Emperor, was Chief of Staff to the Left Army under Prince of Yongjia Ziren and Administrator of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lingsun, in the Jinghe era under the Former Deposed Emperor, was chief of staff to the left army under Prince of Yongjia Liu Ziren and administrator of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 太宗以為寧朔將軍、徐州刺史，討薛安都。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming made him General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xuzhou to campaign against Xue Andu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming made him General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of Xuzhou to campaign against Xue Andu.

sentences.zh: 行至淮陽，即與安都合。

translations.literal: When he reached Huaiyang he at once joined Andu.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Huaiyang he immediately joined Andu.

sentences.zh: 弟闡，時為濟陰太守，戍睢陵城，奉順不同安都，安都攻圍不能克。

translations.literal: His younger brother Chan was then Administrator of Jiyin, garrisoning Suiling city; he remained loyal and would not follow Andu, and Andu besieged him without success.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Chan, then administrator of Jiyin, held Suiling city, remained loyal and refused to join Andu, and Andu could not take him by siege.

sentences.zh: 會令孫至，遣往睢陵令說闡降，闡既降，殺之，令孫亦見殺。

translations.literal: When Lingsun arrived he sent someone to Suiling to persuade Chan to surrender; once Chan surrendered he killed him, and Lingsun was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingsun arrived he sent envoys to persuade Chan to surrender; once Chan surrendered he killed him, and Lingsun was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 先是，清河崔諲亦以將吏見知高祖，永初末，為振威將軍、東萊太守。

translations.literal: Earlier, Cui Yin of Qinghe was also known to the Founding Emperor as a military officer; at the end of Yongchu he was General Who Quells Martial Prestige and Administrator of Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Cui Yin of Qinghe had also been known to the Founding Emperor as a military officer; at the end of Yongchu he was General Who Quells Martial Prestige and administrator of Donglai.

sentences.zh: 少帝初，亡命司馬靈期、司馬順之千餘人圍東萊，諲擊之，斬靈期等三十級。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Short-Reigned Emperor's reign, more than a thousand outlaws under Sima Lingqi and Sima Shunzhi besieged Donglai; Yin attacked them and beheaded Lingqi and thirty others.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Shao's reign, over a thousand outlaws under Sima Lingqi and Sima Shunzhi besieged Donglai; Yin attacked them and beheaded Lingqi and thirty others.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉中，至青州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era under Emperor Wen he rose to Inspector of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen in the Yuanjia era he rose to inspector of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：漢之良吏，居官者或長子孫，孫、曹之世，善職者亦二三十載，皆敷政以盡民和，興讓以存簡久。

translations.literal: The historian says: Among Han's good officials, some held office long enough to see their sons and grandsons grow up; in the Sun and Cao eras capable men also served twenty or thirty years, all spreading governance to achieve popular harmony and promoting yielding to preserve simplicity and endurance.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Among Han's good officials, some held office long enough to see sons and grandsons grow up; in the Sun and Cao eras capable men also served twenty or thirty years, spreading good governance to harmonize the people and promoting modesty to preserve lasting simplicity.

sentences.zh: 及晚代風烈漸衰，非才有起伏，蓋所遭之時異也。

translations.literal: By the late age moral force gradually declined; it was not that talent rose and fell, but rather that the times one encountered differed.
translations.idiomatic: By later ages moral stature had gradually waned; it was not that talent waxed and waned, but that the times men lived in were different.

sentences.zh: 劉道產之在漢南，歷年逾十，惠化流於樊沔，頗有前世遺風，故能樹績垂名，斯為美矣！

translations.literal: Liu Daochan's tenure south of the Han lasted more than ten years; his benevolence spread through Fan and Mian, retaining much of the style of earlier ages—thus he could establish achievement and leave a lasting name; this is truly admirable!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daochan's tenure south of the Han lasted more than ten years; his kindness spread through Fan and Mian, preserving much of an earlier age's spirit—so he could build lasting achievement and renown. This is truly admirable!
